tools.name: ats_jobs_scraper
tools.description:
Job postings API for company career pages: live jobs from Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday, iCIMS and 14 more ATS, with salary when posted. Pay per job.
Runs the Apify Actor cleanyield/ats-jobs-scraper (https://apify.com/cleanyield/ats-jobs-scraper) on your Apify account and returns one JSON item per open job. Main fields: company, ats, title, department, location, countryCode, workplaceType, employmentType, seniority, salaryMin, salaryMax, salaryCurrency (when the posting has a salary), postedAt, url, applyUrl, descriptionText.
Price charged today (Apify Store, pay per result, checked 2026-11-11): USD 0.002 on the Apify Free plan (down to USD 0.0012 on higher plans) per job (USD 2 per 1,000 on the Free plan), plus USD 0.005 per run (Actor start, per GB of memory, minimum one). From 2026-11-24 the price per job changes to USD 0.005 on the Apify Free plan (down to USD 0.003 on higher plans). Optional extras, charged only when you turn them on: Company checked (monitor): USD 0.004 on the Apify Free plan (down to USD 0.0025 on higher plans) (Monitor mode only: each company board checked successfully); Pro mode job: USD 0.005 on the Apify Free plan (down to USD 0.0025 on higher plans) (Extra per job with Pro mode (hiring score, why now, trend, tech stack, AI insight)); Company details: USD 0.01 on the Apify Free plan (down to USD 0.007 on higher plans) (Extra per company with useful details from its website (only when found)). Failed or not-found inputs are not charged. Needs APIFY_TOKEN.
Example arguments: {"companies":["anthropic","https://jobs.lever.co/spotify"],"maxJobsPerCompany":5,"keywords":["engineer"]}

companies.description: Companies. One company per line. Accepted: a company name (Stripe, Scale AI), the company website (figma.com — the Actor follows its Careers link to the job board), a job board URL (https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/anthropic, https://jobs.lever.co/spotify, https://jobs.eu.lever.co/<company>, https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/ramp, https://bunq.recruitee.com, https://<company>.jobs.personio.de, https://<company>.teamtailor.com, https://nvidia.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/NVIDIAExternalCareerSite, https://<tenant>.fa.<dc>.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/<site>, https://<company>.eightfold.ai/careers, a Phenom careers portal such as https://talent.lowes.com/us/en/search-results), the company's own careers page (https://www.figma.com/careers), or a prefixed token (greenhouse:stripe, lever:palantir, lever-eu:<company>, ashby:openai, recruitee:bunq, personio:<company>, teamtailor:<company>). For a bare name the Actor tries Greenhouse and Ashby first, then Lever, then Recruitee, Personio and Teamtailor. Workday, Oracle Recruiting Cloud, Eightfold and Phenom sites need their URL or the company website (emerson.com, bostonscientific.com, lowes.com). Example: ["anthropic", "https://jobs.lever.co/spotify", "ashby:ramp"]. Can be left empty when you use a saved list (see "Saved list name").

savedListName.description: Saved list name (optional). Give your company list a name (e.g. "my-target-accounts") and the Actor remembers it: next runs and schedules use the saved companies plus any you add here. Stored in your own Apify account (key-value store "saved-lists"). Leave empty to use only the companies above.

saveList.description: Save new companies into the saved list. With a saved list name: add the companies of this run to the saved list. Turn off to use the saved list without changing it.

maxJobsPerCompany.description: Max jobs per company. Maximum jobs returned per company after filters, newest first. 0 = all open jobs. Use it to cap cost on big employers (some have 800+ open jobs). Example: 50.

maxResults.description: Max results per run. Stop after this many jobs in total across all companies. 0 = no limit. You pay only for jobs actually returned. Example: 1000.

keywords.description: Keywords. Keep only jobs whose title contains at least one of these words or phrases (case-insensitive; 'engineer' also matches 'Engineering'; words of 3 letters or less like 'AI' or 'QA' match whole words only). Leave empty for all jobs. Example: ["engineer", "data scientist"].

keywordScope.description:
Search keywords in. Where to look for the keywords: only the job title (precise, default) or the title and the full description (broader, e.g. to find every job that mentions 'Kubernetes').
Options: title = Job title only; titleAndDescription = Title and description.

excludeKeywords.description: Exclude keywords. Drop jobs whose title contains any of these words. Example: ["intern", "senior director"].

locations.description: Locations. Keep jobs in any of these places: a city (London), a US state or region code (CA), a country name or ISO code (Germany, DE, United States) or the word 'remote'. Matches the main location and every additional location of the job. Example: ["United States", "London", "remote"].

excludeLocations.description: Exclude locations. City, state code, country name or ISO code, or "remote". A job is dropped only when ALL its locations match (a job in "London | Remote US" stays if you exclude UK). Example: ["India"].

workplaceTypes.description:
Workplace type. Keep only remote, hybrid and/or on-site jobs. Jobs whose ATS does not say the workplace type (and whose location does not mention it) are excluded when this filter is set. Example: ["remote"].
Options: remote = Remote; hybrid = Hybrid; onsite = On-site.

departments.description: Departments or teams. Keep jobs whose department or team contains any of these texts (case-insensitive). Example: ["engineering", "sales"].

employmentTypes.description:
Employment type. Keep only these employment types (normalized across ATS): full_time, part_time, contract, internship, temporary, other. Jobs with unknown type are excluded when this filter is set. Example: ["full_time"].
Options: full_time = Full-time; part_time = Part-time; contract = Contract; internship = Internship; temporary = Temporary; other = Other.

postedWithinDays.description: Posted within the last N days. Keep only jobs published in the last N days (by the ATS publish date). 0 = any date. Example: 7.

postedAfter.description: Posted on or after (exact date). Keep only jobs published on or after this exact date or time (ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-10-01 or 2026-10-01T09:00:00Z), or a relative time like "48 hours" or "7 days". Jobs without a publish date are left out. Empty = any date.

minSalary.description: Minimum annual salary. Keep only jobs whose published salary range reaches at least this amount per year (hourly and monthly pay are annualized). Compared in the currency below, without conversion. Jobs without a published salary are excluded unless you tick the next option. 0 = no salary filter. Example: 150000.

salaryCurrency.description: Salary currency. ISO 4217 currency of the minimum salary (USD, EUR, GBP, CAD…). Only jobs paid in this currency pass the salary filter. Example: USD.

includeJobsWithoutSalary.description: Keep jobs without a published salary. With a minimum salary set: also keep jobs that do not publish a salary.

onlyWithSalary.description: Only jobs with a published salary. Keep only jobs that publish a salary (structured from the ATS or an explicit range in the job text).

seniorities.description:
Seniority. Keep only these levels, read from the job title: intern, entry (junior, new grad, I), mid (II, intermediate), senior (senior, III), lead (staff, principal, lead), director (director, head of), executive (VP, chief). Titles without a level are excluded when this filter is set. Example: ["intern", "entry"] for students and freshers.
Options: intern = Intern; entry = Entry / junior; mid = Mid; senior = Senior; lead = Lead / staff / principal; director = Director / head of; executive = Executive (VP, C-level).

maxExperienceYears.description: Max years of experience required. Drop jobs that ask for MORE than N years of experience (read from phrases like "5+ years of experience"). Jobs that do not say are kept. Example: 2 for freshers and early-career.

onlyVisaSponsorship.description: Only jobs that say they sponsor visas. Keep only jobs whose text explicitly says visa sponsorship is offered ("we sponsor visas", "visa sponsorship is available").

includeDescription.description:
Job description. Include the full job description as clean plain text (default, best for AI and spreadsheets), as the original HTML, both, or none (smaller output).
Options: text = Clean text; html = HTML; both = Text and HTML; none = None.

outputFormat.description:
Output field names. standard = this Actor's fields (recommended). leader-compatible = the field names used by the most popular career-site job APIs on the Store (title, organization, date_posted, locations_alt, countries_derived, ai_salary_min_value, ai_work_arrangement, description_text…) so you can switch without changing your integration. Values still come from the ATS, not from AI.
Options: standard = Standard (recommended); leader-compatible = Compatible with other career-site job APIs.

includeAtsFields.description: Add ATS-specific fields. Also return the fields only each ATS publishes (no extra cost): Greenhouse requisition ID, department path, offices, every pay range and custom fields; Lever commitment, level and the posting's requirement lists as bullets; Ashby compensation tiers with equity, commission and bonus, and secondary locations; Workday requisition ID, exact posting date, time type and hiring entity. Off = the standard fields only (same output as before).

monitorMode.description: Monitor mode (only new or changed jobs). For scheduled runs: remember the jobs found last time (per company) and output only jobs that are new or changed (title, location, salary, workplace type…) since the previous run. Each item has changeType new or changed (and changedFields). You pay only for new/changed jobs plus a small fee per company checked. Schedule the Actor daily or weekly from the Schedules tab.

monitorStateName.description: Monitor state name. Optional name of the storage that keeps the previous results. Use the same name across scheduled runs to compare against them. Leave empty to derive it automatically from your filters (so you can add companies to the list without losing history). Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only. Example: my-watchlist-daily.

includeClosedJobs.description: Also report closed jobs. In monitor mode: also output jobs that disappeared from the board since the last run (changeType closed). Closed jobs count as results. Never reported for a company that could not be read or was cut by 'Max jobs per company'.

skipExistingOnFirstRun.description: First run: save baseline only. In monitor mode: on the first run for a company, store its current jobs as the baseline without outputting or charging them, so you are alerted only about jobs posted from now on.

notifyWebhookUrl.description: Webhook URL for alerts. Optional. When monitor mode finds new or changed jobs, POST a JSON summary (title, lines, items with jobId, company, title, location, salary, url) to this URL. Works with Zapier, Make and n8n (use it to send emails too). Example: https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/catch/123/abc

notifySlackWebhookUrl.description: Slack webhook URL for alerts. Optional. Slack incoming-webhook URL to receive a message when monitor mode finds new or changed jobs (per-company hiring summary + the newest jobs). Example: https://hooks.slack.com/services/T000/B000/XXXX

proMode.description: Pro mode. Turns on every extra for each job: company hiring score (0–100), "hiring is accelerating" flag, jobs posted by the company in the last 30 days, hiring trend since you started running it (stored in your account), a "why now" line for sales outreach, technologies mentioned in the job, and a one-sentence AI insight written only from the job's data. Charged as "pro-result" per job on top of the base price.

enrichCompanies.description: Add company details (emails, phones, socials, tech). Reads each hiring company's own website once per run and adds companyDetails to its jobs: primary email and phone, LinkedIn and X profiles, country and website technologies. Charged once per company with useful data ("company-enriched"); companies without a website or without data are free.

proxyConfiguration.description: Proxy configuration. Not needed: these ATS publish their job board feeds openly, so the Actor connects directly (cheaper and faster). Only enable a proxy if your network requires one. Example: {"useApifyProxy": false}.

inputSchema.description: List the companies you want to watch. Each company can be a name (Stripe), a job board URL (https://jobs.lever.co/spotify), a careers page URL (https://www.figma.com/careers) or a prefixed token (greenhouse:anthropic). The Actor detects the ATS (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Recruitee, Personio, Teamtailor, Workday, Oracle Recruiting Cloud, Eightfold or Phenom), reads its public job board feed and returns one normalized item per open job. You pay only for valid jobs returned; companies that are not found are free.

tools.name: company_enrichment_from_website
tools.description:
Company enrichment by domain: emails, phones, social profiles, tech stack and hiring signals from each site. Enrich Google Maps or CRM leads. Pay per company.
Runs the Apify Actor cleanyield/company-enrichment-from-website (https://apify.com/cleanyield/company-enrichment-from-website) on your Apify account and returns one JSON item per company (one per domain). Main fields: domain, companyName, description, country, emails (generic/role), phones (E.164), primaryEmail, primaryPhone, socialProfiles, address, technologies, hiring, latestPosts, contactPageUrl.
Price charged today (Apify Store, pay per result, checked 2026-11-11): USD 0.01 on the Apify Free plan (down to USD 0.007 on higher plans) per company (USD 10 per 1,000 on the Free plan). From 2026-11-24 the price per company changes to USD 0.01 on the Apify Free plan (down to USD 0.0075 on higher plans). Optional extras, charged only when you turn them on: Pro mode company: USD 0.02 on the Apify Free plan (down to USD 0.014 on higher plans) (Extra per company returned with Pro mode (buying intent score, size, ICP fit, why now, trend, AI insight)). Failed or not-found inputs are not charged. Needs APIFY_TOKEN.
Example arguments: {"domains":["stripe.com","notion.so"]}

domains.description: Domains or website URLs. Company domains or website URLs, one per line. Accepts 'acme.com', 'www.acme.com', 'https://acme.com/about' or even an email like 'info@acme.com' (its domain is used). Duplicates are removed. Bulk is fine: thousands per run. Example: plausible.io Also accepts "startUrls" or "urls" (same format as other contact scrapers). Have a Google Maps export? Use "Google Maps leads or spreadsheet rows" below.

sections.description:
Sections to return. Which parts of the company profile to collect. Fewer sections = fewer pages read and faster runs. companyName, description, language, country and address are always included. Options: contacts (emails and phones), social (LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, GitHub), technologies (tech stack), hiring (careers page, ATS, open roles), posts (latest blog posts). Default: all. Example: ["contacts", "social"]
Options: contacts = Contacts (emails and phones); social = Social profiles; technologies = Technologies (tech stack); hiring = Hiring signals (careers, ATS, open roles); posts = Latest blog posts.

includePersonalEmails.description: Include personal emails. Off by default (GDPR-friendly): only generic and role inboxes are returned (info@, hello@, sales@, ventas@, support@...). Emails that look like a person's (jane@, j.smith@) are omitted and only counted in personalEmailsOmitted. Turn on to include them, each marked with type 'personal'. If you turn it on, you are responsible for having a legal basis to process them.

maxPagesPerDomain.description: Max pages per domain. Hard cap of pages read per company: the home page plus the pages most likely to have contact data (contact, legal notice/Impressum, privacy policy, about, team, terms) and the careers, blog/feed and sitemap pages, all found through same-site links and common paths in English, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French and Italian. Default 10 (median 1.8 s per company). The price per company does not change with this value.

maxPosts.description: Max blog posts per company. How many of the latest blog posts (title, URL, ISO date) to return per company, from its RSS/Atom feed or blog page. 0 disables posts. Example: 5.

domainTimeoutSecs.description: Time limit per domain (seconds). Maximum time spent on one company. When reached, the Actor returns what it already found (if valid). Keeps sync calls from Clay, n8n or Make under ~20 s. Example: 15.

maxResults.description: Maximum results. Stop after this many companies are returned. Use it to cap cost on big lists; you only pay for companies actually returned. Leave empty for no limit. Example: 1000.

maxConcurrency.description: Domains in parallel. How many companies are processed at the same time (each one on its own host, with at most a few requests in parallel per site). Example: 10.

respectRobotsTxt.description: Respect robots.txt. On by default: every host is checked against its own robots.txt; pages disallowed for all crawlers are never requested, a Crawl-delay is respected (fewer pages are read when it does not fit in the per-domain time limit), and sites whose home page is disallowed are reported as robots_disallowed (not charged).

rows.description: Google Maps leads or spreadsheet rows (JSON). Paste the rows exported by a Google Maps scraper as they are (JSON), or any spreadsheet rows with a website column. The website column is detected automatically (website, url, domain, site…); city, street/address, postal code and country code are used to read the right branch page. Rows without a website, or whose website is a Google Maps link, a social profile or a delivery/booking aggregator, are skipped and not charged. Rows with the same website are returned and charged once. Every result keeps the original row in "row". This Actor does not scrape Google Maps: it reads each business's own website.

csvUrl.description: CSV or Google Sheet URL. Link to a CSV file (for example a Google Maps export) or a Google Sheet shared as "Anyone with the link". Same rules as the JSON rows: the website column is detected automatically and the other columns are returned unchanged in "row". Example: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit

datasetId.description: Dataset ID (chain after a Google Maps scraper run). Enrich the businesses found by another run in your Apify account: paste the dataset ID from its Storage tab. Each item is one row; its fields are returned in "row". Example: aBcD1234EfGh

websiteColumn.description: Website column. Name of the column with the website in your rows, CSV or dataset. Leave empty to detect it automatically. Example: website

proMode.description: Pro mode (buying signals, scores, AI insight). One checkbox for all the extras: buying-intent score 0–100 with the signals behind it (hiring, open roles, recent posts, sales/marketing tools, and in monitor mode new tools, new posts or started hiring), estimated company size, ICP fit score against your ideal customer, a 'why now' line for sales, the trend since you started monitoring, and a one-sentence AI insight per company. Charged as an extra event per company (see Pricing). Off by default.

idealCustomer.description: Ideal customer profile (optional). Optional criteria for your ideal customer. Each company gets "icpScore" (0–100 = share of your criteria it meets); turn on "Only return companies that match" to filter, and Pro mode shows which criteria matched or missed. Keys (all optional): countries (ISO-2 list), languages (ISO 639-1 list), technologies (any of these, e.g. ["Shopify","HubSpot"]), excludeTechnologies, mustBeHiring, minOpenRoles, keywords (in name or description), sizes (["11-50","51-200"]), mustHaveContact.

screenByIdealCustomer.description: Only return companies that match my ideal customer. With an ideal customer profile: return (and charge the normal price for) only companies whose icpScore is at least the minimum below. Companies below it are not returned, are listed in the key-value store record SCREENED_OUT and are not charged today (a small screening fee per screened company may be added later, always announced in advance on the Pricing tab). Failed sites are free.

minIcpScore.description: Minimum ICP score to return a company. 0–100. 100 (default) = the company meets all your criteria; 50 = at least half of them.

monitorMode.description: Monitor mode (only new or changed companies). For scheduled runs: remember each company's last profile and output only companies that are new or changed since the previous run, with a list of changes (started hiring, open roles changed, technology added/removed, new blog post, contact added/removed, social profile changed). You pay for each new/changed company returned and, starting November 24, 2026, USD 0.005 per watched company per monitor run (failed sites are free). Schedule the Actor daily or weekly from the Schedules tab.

monitorStateName.description: Monitor state name. Optional name of the storage that keeps the previous profiles. Use the same name across scheduled runs to compare against them. Leave empty to derive it automatically from the domain list and sections. Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only. Example: my-accounts-weekly.

notifyWebhookUrl.description: Webhook URL for alerts. Optional. When monitor mode finds changes, POST a JSON summary (companies and their changes) to this URL (works with Zapier, Make, n8n). Example: https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/catch/123/abc

notifySlackWebhookUrl.description: Slack webhook URL for alerts. Optional. Slack incoming-webhook URL to receive a message when monitor mode finds changes, e.g. 'Acme (acme.com): Started hiring (12 open roles); Added HubSpot'. Example: https://hooks.slack.com/services/T000/B000/XXXX

savedListName.description: Saved list name. Optional. Give your list of companies a name and the Actor remembers it: the next runs (for example scheduled ones) enrich the saved list plus any new domains you add, without pasting it again.

saveList.description: Add new domains to the saved list. When a saved list name is set, add the domains of this run to it (on by default).

proxyConfiguration.description: Proxy configuration. Optional. By default company websites are read directly (no proxy), which works for almost all sites and keeps cost low. Sites that block automated requests are reported as blocked and not charged; the Actor never tries to bypass bot challenges. Example: {"useApifyProxy": false}

outputFormat.description:
Output format. 'standard' (default): our clean company profile. 'leader-compatible': the field names popular contact scrapers use (emails and phones as string lists, linkedIns, twitters, facebooks, instagrams, youtubes, tiktoks, pinterests, whatsapps...), one row per company, with our extra fields next to them (emailDetails, phoneDetails, technologies, hiring...). Use it to switch without changing your integration.
Options: standard = Standard company profile; leader-compatible = Compatible with other contact scrapers (field names).

startUrls.description: Start URLs (alias of domains). Same as "domains", accepted so you can reuse the input of other contact scrapers ([{"url": "https://acme.com"}]). Each start URL is one company.

maxRequestsPerStartUrl.description: Max pages per start URL (alias). Alias of maxPagesPerDomain, accepted for compatibility with other contact scrapers.

inputSchema.description: Give a list of company domains or website URLs. Each company that can be read returns ONE dataset item (one row per company, fixed price per company, never per page). Sites that are down, parked, blocked (403, Cloudflare challenge) or have no usable data are not charged and are listed in the FAILED_DOMAINS record of the key-value store.

tools.name: app_store_google_play_reviews
tools.description:
Returns App Store and Google Play reviews: rating, title, text, date, app version, developer reply. iOS and Android reviews scraper, USD 0.10 per 1,000.
Runs the Apify Actor cleanyield/app-store-google-play-reviews (https://apify.com/cleanyield/app-store-google-play-reviews) on your Apify account and returns one JSON item per review. Main fields: store, appId, appName, country, language, rating, title, text, date, appVersion, authorName, developerReply, thumbsUp, url.
Price charged today (Apify Store, pay per result, checked 2026-11-11): USD 0.0001 on the Apify Free plan (down to USD 0.00008 on higher plans) per review (USD 0.1 per 1,000 on the Free plan). Optional extras, charged only when you turn them on: App monitored: USD 0.005 on the Apify Free plan (down to USD 0.0035 on higher plans) (Each app checked in monitor mode, per run); App insights: USD 0.01 on the Apify Free plan (down to USD 0.007 on higher plans) (Actionable alerts for an app with enough data to compare); Pro mode review: USD 0.002 on the Apify Free plan (down to USD 0.0014 on higher plans) (Extra per review that received the AI sentence in Pro mode). Failed or not-found inputs are not charged. Needs APIFY_TOKEN.
Example arguments: {"apps":["https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.duolingo"],"maxReviewsPerApp":20}

apps.description: Apps (App Store and/or Google Play). One app per line. Accepts App Store URLs (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/instagram/id389801252), App Store numeric ids (389801252), Google Play URLs (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.instagram.android) and Android package names (com.instagram.android). To pass an iOS bundle id, prefix it: appstore:com.burbn.instagram. Both stores can be mixed in one run. For competitor comparison, list your own app first, then competitors. Not required if you use a saved list (savedListName). Inputs written for other popular review scrapers also work (appIds, startUrls, country, language, maxItems, sort): see 'Migrating from other scrapers' in the README.

countries.description: Countries (App Store). Two-letter App Store country codes. App Store reviews are separate per country storefront, so each country is fetched separately (up to ~500 most recent reviews per country, an Apple limit). The first country is also used for the Google Play listing. Example: us, gb, ca, au, de, br, ar. Default if empty: us.

languages.description: Languages (Google Play). Google Play groups reviews by language, not by country. Each language is fetched separately. Use codes like en, es, pt, de, fr, ja, pt-BR. Example: en, es. Default if empty: en.

devices.description: Devices (Google Play). Google Play keeps separate reviews per device. phone (default) is what the store shows first. Add tablet, chromebook, watch, tv or car to also get reviews written on those devices (each device is fetched separately and every review has a device field). Example: phone, tablet. Default if empty: phone.

maxReviewsPerApp.description: Maximum reviews per app (per country / language). Stop after this many reviews for each app in each App Store country or Google Play language (counting only reviews that pass your filters). Caps your cost: you pay only for reviews returned. App Store gives at most ~500 recent reviews per country. In monitor mode this caps how many new reviews a run can return. Example: 200. Default if empty: 500.

sortBy.description:
Sort order. newest = most recent first (default, required for monitor mode and for date filters to stop early). mostHelpful = reviews with the most helpful votes first (on Google Play this is the store's 'Most relevant' order). For only 5-star or only 1-star reviews, use the star filters instead of a sort. rating = highest stars first (Google Play only; App Store falls back to newest). Default if empty: newest.
Options: newest = Newest first; mostHelpful = Most helpful first; rating = Highest rating first (Google Play only).

minRating.description: Minimum stars. Only return reviews with at least this many stars (1–5). Leave empty for all. Example: 4 to collect positive reviews for testimonials.

maxRating.description: Maximum stars. Only return reviews with at most this many stars (1–5). Example: 2 to get only negative reviews (1–2★) for your support team. Use the same value in minimum and maximum to get exactly one star level (filtered server-side on Google Play).

reviewsSince.description: Only reviews since. Only return reviews written or edited on or after this date. Accepts a date (2026-10-01) or a relative period (7 days, 2 weeks, 3 months). With newest-first sorting the Actor stops paging as soon as it passes this date, so it is fast and cheap. Example: 30 days.

reviewsUntil.description: Only reviews until. Only return reviews written or edited on or before this date (a date alone includes that whole day). Accepts 2026-10-31 or a relative period (7 days). Combine with 'Only reviews since' for a date range. Example: 2026-10-31.

keywords.description: Keywords. Only return reviews whose title or text contains at least one of these words or phrases (case- and accent-insensitive). You pay only for matching reviews. Example: crash, refund, battery.

appVersions.description: App versions. Only return reviews written on these app versions. A version also matches its sub-versions: 2.1 matches 2.1.3. Reviews without a version are excluded when this is set. Example: 8.12, 8.13.

omitAuthorNames.description: Omit reviewer names (privacy). On by default: authorName is always null, so the output contains no personal names (data minimization). Turn it off only if you need the public display name of each reviewer, for example to reply to them.

monitorMode.description: Monitor mode (only new reviews). For scheduled runs: remember the reviews already seen and output only new ones (changeType=new) and reviews whose author edited the rating or text (changeType=changed). You pay only for those, plus a small per-app check fee. The first run saves a baseline. Schedule the Actor daily or weekly from the Schedules tab. Forces newest-first sorting.

monitorStateName.description: Monitor state name. Optional name of the storage that keeps the reviews already seen. Use the same name across scheduled runs to compare against them. Leave empty to derive it automatically from the apps, countries, languages and star filters. Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only. Example: my-app-reviews-daily.

notifyWebhookUrl.description: Webhook URL for alerts. Optional. When monitor mode finds new reviews, POST a JSON summary (title, lines, items with negative reviews first) to this URL. Works with Zapier, Make and n8n (use it to send emails too). Example: https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/catch/123/abc

notifySlackWebhookUrl.description: Slack webhook URL for alerts. Optional. Slack incoming-webhook URL. In monitor mode you get a message with the new 1–2★ reviews (stars, app, store, version, text and link) and the actionable alerts. Example: https://hooks.slack.com/services/T000/B000/XXXX

notifyOnlyNegative.description: Alert only when there are negative reviews. If on, the webhook/Slack alert is sent only when the run found new 1–2★ reviews or an actionable alert. If off, you are notified whenever there are new reviews.

proMode.description: Pro mode: topics, urgency score, AI conclusion and suggested replies (paid add-on). One checkbox for all extras. Each review gets: topics (crashes_bugs, payments_billing, login_account, ads, performance, ux_design, update_regression, customer_support, privacy_security, notifications, missing_feature, praise), priorityScore (0–100 urgency to sort your support queue), insight (one-sentence AI conclusion based only on the review), suggestedReply (AI reply draft for 1–3★ reviews, in the review's language) and appDetails (developer, developer website, category, store rating, reputation score 0–100 and rating trend). Also turns on the actionable alerts and competitor comparison below. The Pro fee is charged only for reviews that received the AI conclusion. Off by default: the basic run stays cheap and fast.

generateReport.description: Actionable alerts and competitor comparison (paid add-on). Deterministic alerts per app: spike of 1–2★ reviews vs the previous week, average rating drop week over week, a new app version rated lower than the previous one, negative Google Play reviews left without a developer reply, and how your app (the first app of each store in the list) ranks against the competitors you listed. Stored as REPORT (JSON) and REPORT_MD (Markdown) and included in monitor alerts. Charged per app only when there is enough data to compare.

outputFormat.description:
Output format. standard = this Actor's fields (recommended). leader-compatible = the field names used by other popular review scrapers (id, userName, date, score, scoreText, title, text, replyText, replyDate, version, thumbsUp, criterias, url, appId, country, language), plus reviewId, store, appName and schemaVersion, so you can switch without changing your integration.
Options: standard = Standard; leader-compatible = Compatible with other popular review scrapers.

maxTotalReviews.description: Maximum reviews for the whole run. Optional cap for the entire run across all apps, countries, languages and devices (maxReviewsPerApp caps each one). Leave empty for no total cap. Example: 1000.

savedListName.description: Saved list name. Optional. Give your list of apps a name (for example my-competitors) and the Actor remembers it: next runs with the same name use the saved apps plus any you add in 'apps', so scheduled runs need no edits. Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens.

saveList.description: Save apps to the list. If on (default), apps typed in 'apps' are added to the saved list. Turn off to use the saved list without changing it.

proxyConfiguration.description: Proxy configuration. Not needed: both stores answer without a proxy. If a store starts blocking, the Actor automatically retries through Apify datacenter proxy. Set a proxy here only if you want to force one.

inputSchema.description: List the apps whose reviews you want (App Store and Google Play can be mixed). Each valid review is one dataset item and one charged result; failed or incomplete reviews are never charged. Turn on monitor mode and schedule the Actor to get only new reviews, with alerts on negative ones.

tools.name: fmcsa_carrier_data
tools.description:
Returns carrier records from official FMCSA data: USDOT, MC, authority, insurance on file when available, safety, phone. FMCSA carrier lookup. Pay per result.
Runs the Apify Actor cleanyield/fmcsa-carrier-data (https://apify.com/cleanyield/fmcsa-carrier-data) on your Apify account and returns one JSON item per carrier. Main fields: dotNumber, mcNumbers, legalName, dbaName, entityType, usdotStatus, authorityStatus, physicalAddress, phone, email, powerUnits, drivers, cargoCarried, insurancePolicies (when on file), safetyRating, addDate, fmcsaUrl.
Price charged today (Apify Store, pay per result, checked 2026-11-11): USD 0.005 on the Apify Free plan (down to USD 0.0035 on higher plans) per carrier (USD 5 per 1,000 on the Free plan). Optional extras, charged only when you turn them on: Pro mode carrier: USD 0.005 on the Apify Free plan (Extra per carrier with Pro mode (risk score, insurance renewal, why now, trend, AI insight)); Company website: USD 0.01 on the Apify Free plan (Extra per carrier whose own website was read successfully). Failed or not-found inputs are not charged. Needs APIFY_TOKEN.
Example arguments: {"states":["TX"],"addedWithinDays":7,"maxResults":10}

dotNumbers.description: USDOT numbers (bulk lookup). USDOT numbers to look up, one per line (leading zeros and 'USDOT' prefixes are fine). Example: 80806. When you give USDOT or MC numbers, the search filters below are ignored and every number is returned regardless of status. Numbers that don't exist are reported in the log and never charged.

mcNumbers.description: MC / FF / MX docket numbers (bulk lookup). Operating authority docket numbers, one per line. Accepts 'MC-135797', 'MC135797', 'FF51075' or just '135797' (MC is assumed). Example: MC-135797.

states.description: States. Physical (domicile) state of the company: 2-letter codes or full names. Example: TX, OK. Leave empty for all states.

cities.description: Cities. Physical city names (exact match, case-insensitive). Combine with States to avoid same-name cities elsewhere. Example: Dallas.

zipCodes.description: ZIP codes or prefixes. Physical ZIP codes (5 digits) or prefixes (3–4 digits match a whole area). Example: 75201 or 752.

nearLocation.description: Near a ZIP or city (radius search). Find carriers based within a radius of a 5-digit ZIP (75201) or a city with its state (Dallas, TX). Uses US Census ZIP centroids, no extra cost. Each result gets distanceMiles. Combine with any filter below (fleet size, cargo, new carriers...).

radiusMiles.description: Radius (miles). Radius around 'Near a ZIP or city', 1 to 300 miles. Default 50.

nameContains.description: Company name contains. Optional text that must appear in the legal name or DBA name (case-insensitive). Example: logistics.

entityTypes.description:
Entity types. Keep only entities registered as any of these types (FMCSA 'carship' field). Example: carrier for trucking companies, broker for freight brokers. Leave empty for all.
Options: carrier = Carrier (trucking company); broker = Broker; freightForwarder = Freight forwarder; shipper = Shipper; intermodalEquipmentProvider = Intermodal equipment provider; cargoTankFacility = Cargo tank facility; registrant = Registrant.

operationType.description:
Operation type. Interstate (crosses state lines, most for-hire trucking) or intrastate carriers. Example: interstate.
Options: any = Any; interstate = Interstate; intrastate = Intrastate (all); intrastateHazmat = Intrastate hazmat; intrastateNonHazmat = Intrastate non-hazmat.

authorizedForHireOnly.description: Only authorized for-hire carriers. Keep only companies whose operation classification includes 'Authorized for hire' (they haul freight for others — the ones brokers book and insurers quote). Excludes private fleets.

hazmat.description:
Hazmat. Filter by the hazardous-materials flag. Example: only (hazmat carriers only).
Options: any = Any; only = Only hazmat carriers; exclude = Exclude hazmat carriers.

cargoTypes.description:
Cargo carried. Keep carriers that haul any of these cargo types (as declared on their MCS-150). Example: refrigeratedFood for reefer carriers.
Options: generalFreight = General Freight; householdGoods = Household Goods; metalSheetsCoilsRolls = Metal: sheets, coils, rolls; motorVehicles = Motor Vehicles; driveTowAway = Drive/Tow away; logsPolesBeamsLumber = Logs, Poles, Beams, Lumber; buildingMaterials = Building Materials; mobileHomes = Mobile Homes; machineryLargeObjects = Machinery, Large Objects; freshProduce = Fresh Produce; liquidsGases = Liquids/Gases; intermodalContainers = Intermodal Containers; passengers = Passengers; oilfieldEquipment = Oilfield Equipment; livestock = Livestock; grainFeedHay = Grain, Feed, Hay; coalCoke = Coal/Coke; meat = Meat; garbageRefuse = Garbage/Refuse; usMail = US Mail; chemicals = Chemicals; commoditiesDryBulk = Commodities Dry Bulk; refrigeratedFood = Refrigerated Food; beverages = Beverages; paperProducts = Paper Products; utilities = Utilities; agriculturalFarmSupplies = Agricultural/Farm Supplies; construction = Construction; waterWell = Water Well; other = Other.

minPowerUnits.description: Minimum power units (trucks). Minimum number of power units (trucks/tractors) reported on the MCS-150. Example: 5.

maxPowerUnits.description: Maximum power units (trucks). Maximum number of power units. Example: 1 for owner-operators, 10 for small fleets.

minDrivers.description: Minimum drivers. Minimum total drivers reported on the MCS-150. Example: 2.

maxDrivers.description: Maximum drivers. Maximum total drivers. Example: 20.

addedWithinDays.description: Added in the last N days. Only companies whose USDOT number was added (registered) in the last N days — relative to each run, ideal for scheduled 'new carriers' feeds. Example: 30. FMCSA publishes new registrations with a 1–2 day delay.

addedSince.description:
Added on or after (date). Only companies registered (USDOT add date) on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2026-10-01. If 'Added in the last N days' is also set, the more recent date wins.
Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

addedBefore.description:
Added on or before (date). Only companies registered on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2026-10-31.
Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

mcs150UpdatedSince.description:
MCS-150 updated since (date). Only companies that filed or updated their MCS-150 registration form on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2026-09-01 (recently active companies).
Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

usdotStatus.description:
USDOT status. Registration status of the USDOT number. Default: active (operating companies). Not applied to USDOT/MC lookups.
Options: active = Active; inactive = Inactive; pending = Pending; any = Any.

authorityStatus.description:
Operating authority (MC). Filter by operating authority: 'active' = has an active MC/FF/MX authority (for-hire interstate carriers and brokers); 'none' = no authority docket (private fleets, intrastate).
Options: any = Any; active = Active MC/FF/MX authority; none = No authority.

safetyRatings.description:
Safety ratings. Keep only these FMCSA safety ratings. Most carriers are 'unrated'. Example: conditional, unsatisfactory (to vet risky carriers).
Options: satisfactory = Satisfactory; conditional = Conditional; unsatisfactory = Unsatisfactory; unrated = Not rated.

requireEmail.description: Only with email. Keep only companies that published an email address on their FMCSA registration.

requirePhone.description: Only with phone. Keep only companies that published a phone number.

sortBy.description:
Sort by. Order of the search results. Newest = most recently registered first.
Options: newest = Newest registrations first; largestFleet = Largest fleet first; recentlyUpdated = Most recent MCS-150 update first; dotNumber = USDOT number.

maxResults.description: Maximum results. Search mode: stop after this many carriers. Use it to cap your cost: you pay only for results actually returned. USDOT/MC lookups always return every number you list. Example: 1000.

maxResultsPerState.description: Max results per state. Optional cap per state when you select several states (e.g. 200 per state). 0 or empty = no per-state cap (maxResults still caps the whole run).

authorityEvents.description:
Authority events (new authority, revocations...). Daily feed from FMCSA's authority history: get the carriers and brokers whose operating authority was GRANTED, newly applied for (pending), reinstated, suspended, revoked, withdrawn or put out of service in the last N days, with the event in authorityEvent. Combine with state, radius, fleet and cargo filters. Schedule it daily with monitor mode to get only the new ones.
Options: granted = Granted (new authority); pending = Pending (new application); reinstated = Reinstated; suspended = Suspended; revoked = Revoked / inactivated; withdrawn = Withdrawn; outOfService = Out of service.

authorityEventsWithinDays.description: Events in the last N days. How far back to read authority events. 1 = yesterday and today (for a daily schedule). Default 7, max 365.

includeAuthority.description: Include operating authority details. Add out-of-service order status, each carrier's operating authorities (type and status per MC docket) and insurance requirements vs. on file (BIPD amount, cargo, bond), from FMCSA's Motus and L&I datasets. Free, adds ~1 s per 150 carriers.

includeInsurance.description: Include insurance policies. Add active/pending insurance filings: insurer, policy number, coverage, effective date (renewal timing for insurance agents) and pending cancellation date when published.

includeInsuranceHistory.description: Include insurance history and upcoming cancellations. Cancelled and replaced policies (insurer, policy, dates), the next cancellation already filed with a future date, and cancellations in the last 12 months. Free.

saferLiveCheck.description: Confirm possibly stale statuses on FMCSA SAFER (live). Only rows whose status may be out of date in FMCSA open data (pending authority or pending revocation from the frozen legacy L&I system, USDOT status flagged usdotStatusMaybeStale, or contradictory statuses) are checked live on the official SAFER snapshot: at most 1 request per second and 50 per run. Each row says where its status came from (statusSource, saferCheck). Free.

includeSafety.description: Include inspections, out-of-service rates and crashes (24 months). Add the SAFER-style safety block: roadside inspections (vehicle/driver), out-of-service counts and rates, crashes (fatal/injury/tow-away) for the last 24 months and the 5 public BASIC measures, from FMCSA's monthly SMS snapshot. No extra charge.

checkSharedContacts.description: Flag shared phones and emails. Count how many USDOT records use the same phone and email. 10 or more (typically a permit or compliance agent, sometimes a company's own subsidiaries) sets phoneIsShared/emailIsShared so you can skip agent contacts. No extra charge.

contactData.description:
Contact data. FMCSA publishes the phone and email each company gives for official contact. Choose 'omitForIndividuals' to drop phone/email of sole proprietors (owner-operators registered as individuals), or 'omit' to drop all contact data. Outreach is subject to TCPA and CAN-SPAM.
Options: include = Include phone, mobile, fax and email; omitForIndividuals = Omit for sole proprietors; omit = Omit all contact data.

includeOfficerNames.description: Include company officer names. Add the names of up to 2 company officers listed on the MCS-150 (personal data: off by default).

includeRawData.description: Include the raw census row. Attach every column of the FMCSA Company Census (140+ fields, exactly as filed) in rawCensus. Bigger output; no extra charge.

outputFormat.description:
Output format. leader-compatible adds (never replaces) the field names used by other popular FMCSA scrapers (mcNumber, registrationDate, authorityGrantedDate, currentlyOutOfService, saferSnapshotUrl, cargoTypes, totalDrivers, cellPhone...), so you can switch without changing your integration. See 'Migrating from other scrapers' in the README.
Options: standard = Standard; leader-compatible = Standard + field names used by other popular FMCSA scrapers.

socrataAppToken.description: Socrata app token (optional). Optional free app token from data.transportation.gov (Developer settings) for higher API quota on very large runs. Not needed for normal use: the Actor paces its requests politely without one. E.g. the app token string shown in your data.transportation.gov developer settings.

monitorMode.description: Monitor mode (only new or changed carriers). For scheduled runs: remember what was found last time and output only carriers that are new or changed since the previous run (authority, insurance, fleet size, phone/email, address, name, safety rating). Each item gets changeType (new/changed) and a field-by-field changes list. You pay for each new/changed carrier returned and, starting November 24, 2026, USD 0.001 per watched carrier per monitor run. Schedule the Actor daily or weekly.

monitorStateName.description: Monitor state name. Optional name of the storage that keeps the previous results. Use the same name across scheduled runs to compare against them. Leave empty to derive it automatically from the rest of the input. Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only. Example: tx-new-carriers.

notifyWebhookUrl.description: Webhook URL for alerts. Optional. When monitor mode finds new or changed carriers, POST a JSON summary to this URL (works with Zapier, Make, n8n). Example: https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/catch/123/abc

notifySlackWebhookUrl.description: Slack webhook URL for alerts. Optional. Slack incoming-webhook URL to receive a message listing new and changed carriers. Example: https://hooks.slack.com/services/T000/B000/XXXX

savedListName.description: Saved watchlist name. Give your USDOT/MC list a name (e.g. my-carriers) and the Actor remembers it: next runs use the saved list plus any numbers you add. Pair it with Monitor mode for a carrier watchlist.

saveList.description: Save new numbers to the list. Add the USDOT/MC numbers of this run to the saved list (off = use the saved list without changing it).

proMode.description: Pro mode (risk score, insurance renewal, why-now, trend, AI summary). One checkbox for all the extras: a 0-100 carrier risk score with its reasons, estimated insurance renewal date, a dated 'why now' line for sales outreach, the trend since you started monitoring (fleet, crashes, out-of-service rate) and a one-sentence AI summary per carrier. In monitor mode it also alerts on safety changes. Charged as an extra 'pro-result' event per carrier (see Pricing).

enrichCompanyWebsite.description: Add company website contacts. For carriers whose email uses their own domain (not Gmail/Yahoo...), read the company website and add its emails, phones, contact page, social profiles, technologies and hiring status in companyWebsite. Slower (a few seconds per website). Charged as an extra 'company-website' event only when the website is read successfully.

inputSchema.description: Either paste USDOT / MC numbers to look up (bulk), or use the filters to search the official FMCSA Company Census (state, city, ZIP, entity type, fleet size, date added...). Each carrier found is one dataset item and one charged result. Data comes from FMCSA open data on data.transportation.gov (updated daily).

tools.name: latam_public_tenders
tools.description:
Returns Latin America public tenders (licitaciones) from Colombia, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay, Uruguay: buyer, deadline, USD amount, winner. Pay per result.
Runs the Apify Actor cleanyield/latam-public-tenders (https://apify.com/cleanyield/latam-public-tenders) on your Apify account and returns one JSON item per public tender. Main fields: tenderId, country, source, title, titleEn, description, buyer, categories, procedureType, status, amount (local currency and USD), publishedDate, closingDate, awardees, documents, url.
Price charged today (Apify Store, pay per result, checked 2026-11-11): USD 0.008 on the Apify Free plan (down to USD 0.0062 on higher plans) per tender (USD 8 per 1,000 on the Free plan). Optional extras, charged only when you turn them on: Pro mode tender: USD 0.006 on the Apify Free plan (down to USD 0.0047 on higher plans) (Extra per tender delivered with Pro mode: 0-100 fit score with reasons, days to close and urgency, buyer profile from your monitoring history, why-now line and AI insight sentence (when available)). Failed or not-found inputs are not charged. Needs APIFY_TOKEN.
Example arguments: {"countries":["CO"],"sectors":["it-software"],"status":["open"],"maxResults":10}

countries.description:
Countries. Which official sources to search: CO = Colombia (SECOP II on datos.gov.co), BR = Brazil (PNCP, Portal Nacional de Contratações Públicas), CL = Chile (Mercado Público / ChileCompra OCDS API), PY = Paraguay (DNCP OCDS API), UY = Uruguay (ARCE OCDS open data). Leave empty for CO, BR and CL. Uruguay has no keyword search in its API (each new call is read one by one): wide date ranges are slower there. Example: ["CO", "PY"].
Options: CO = Colombia (SECOP II); BR = Brazil (PNCP); CL = Chile (Mercado Público); PY = Paraguay (DNCP); UY = Uruguay (ARCE).

sectors.description:
Sectors (ready-made keyword + UNSPSC packs). Pick your sector and the Actor matches tenders in Spanish and Portuguese for you (accents ignored), using sector keywords in the title and UNSPSC codes of the main category. Combine with your own keywords. Example: ["it-software"] finds software licences, computers, IT services in all three countries.
Options: it-software = IT, software & computers; construction = Construction & public works; cleaning = Cleaning & facility services; security = Security & surveillance; medical = Medical supplies, drugs & lab; food = Food & catering; vehicles = Vehicles, parts, tyres & fuel; office-supplies = Office supplies & furniture; consulting = Consulting, audit & engineering studies; telecom = Telecom & connectivity; energy = Electrical, lighting & solar energy; events-travel = Events, travel & lodging; training-education = Training & education services; uniforms-ppe = Uniforms, workwear & PPE; waste-environment = Waste management & environment.

keywords.description: Keywords. Words or phrases to find in the tender title, description, category or items (any of them matches; accents and upper/lower case are ignored; matches the start of a word, so 'licencia' also finds 'licencias'). Write them in Spanish for CO/CL/PY/UY and Portuguese for BR. Example: ["ambulancia", "ambulância", "vigilancia"].

excludeKeywords.description: Exclude keywords. Tenders containing any of these words are dropped (noise filter). Example: ["arrendamiento", "locação"].

categoryCodes.description: UNSPSC category codes. UNSPSC codes or prefixes (2, 4, 6 or 8 digits) of the tender's main category: 43 = IT and telecom, 4321 = computers, 72 = construction services, 80111600 = temporary staff. Chile classifies every tender with UNSPSC; Colombia rarely does for open tenders; Brazil does not use UNSPSC (use keywords). When combined with keywords, a tender matches if either matches.

buyers.description: Buying entities. Only tenders from these buyers: part of the name (accents ignored, e.g. 'Universidad Nacional', 'Prefeitura de São Paulo') or tax ID (NIT for Colombia, CNPJ for Brazil, RUT for Chile). Example: ["899999063", "ministerio de obras publicas"].

regions.description: Regions. Buyer location: Colombian department or city (e.g. 'Antioquia', 'Bogotá'), Brazilian state (2-letter code like 'SP' or name), Chilean region (e.g. 'Valparaíso', 'Metropolitana'). Leave empty for the whole country.

minAmountUsd.description: Minimum estimated amount (USD). Only tenders whose estimated budget (or awarded amount) is at least this many US dollars, converted from COP/BRL/CLP with today's exchange rate. Tenders without a published amount are excluded when you set this. Example: 50000.

maxAmountUsd.description: Maximum estimated amount (USD). Only tenders whose estimated budget is at most this many US dollars (e.g. 200000 for SMEs). Tenders without a published amount are excluded when you set this.

status.description: Status. Normalized status across countries: open (accepting bids), closed (bidding closed, under evaluation), awarded, cancelled, unsuccessful (no valid bids / 'desierta'), suspended, unknown. Default: open. Leave empty for any status. Example: ["awarded"] to study who wins.

procurementScope.description:
Procedure scope. competitive (default) = only procedures any supplier can bid on: public tenders, reverse auctions (pregão, subasta inversa), small-value open calls, merit contests, restricted tenders. all = also direct awards, exemptions (dispensa, inexigibilidade, contratación directa), requests for information and asset sales.
Options: competitive = Competitive only (you can bid); all = All procedures.

procedureTypes.description: Procedure types. Optional filter by normalized procedure type, e.g. ["reverse-auction"] for pregão eletrônico / subasta inversa, ["public-tender"] for licitación pública / concorrência. Leave empty for all types in the chosen scope.

publishedWithinDays.description: Published in the last N days. Tenders published in the last N days (default 7). Keep 7 for a daily monitor: Colombia's open data arrives with a 1–4 day delay (tenders show up later with their original publication date) and the overlap is free in monitor mode (already-sent tenders are not charged again). Ignored if 'Published since' is set. Example: 7.

publishedSince.description:
Published since (date). Absolute start date YYYY-MM-DD (buyer's local date). Overrides 'Published in the last N days'. Example: 2026-10-01.
Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

publishedUntil.description:
Published until (date). Optional end date YYYY-MM-DD (buyer's local date, inclusive). Leave empty for 'up to today'.
Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

closingFrom.description:
Closing date from. Only tenders whose bid deadline is on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Example: 2026-11-10.
Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

closingTo.description:
Closing date to. Only tenders whose bid deadline is on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD), e.g. to see what closes this month.
Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

tenderIds.description: Tender IDs (lookup). Look up specific tenders instead of searching (search filters are ignored). Accepts the tenderId from this Actor's output or the id shown on each portal: CO1.REQ.11304903 (SECOP II), 88124961000159-1-000131/2026 (PNCP 'Id contratação PNCP'), 5751-39-LR26 (Mercado Público), ocds-03ad3f-490443-1 (DNCP Paraguay), UY-1384146 (ARCE Uruguay, 'UY-' + purchase id). Ids that don't exist are reported and not charged.

maxResults.description: Maximum results. Stop after this many tenders (shared fairly between countries). Caps your cost: you pay only for tenders actually returned. In monitor mode it caps new/changed tenders. Example: 100.

includeAwardees.description: Include awardees. For awarded tenders, add who won and for how much (company name, tax ID, amount). Costs one extra request per awarded tender in Chile and a few in Brazil (still one charged result). Default on.

awardeeData.description:
Awardee personal data. Awardees can be individuals (sole traders). omitIndividuals (default) hides the name and ID of natural persons and keeps companies; include keeps everything published by the government; omit removes awardee names and IDs entirely.
Options: omitIndividuals = Hide individuals (keep companies); include = Include all; omit = Omit all awardee names/IDs.

includeDetails.description: Include items and documents. Add the line items (description, quantity, unit, category, estimated value) and, for Brazil, the list of tender documents (edital, termo de referência) with direct links. Brazil needs 2 extra requests per tender, so runs are slower. Default off.

translateToEnglish.description: English titles (titleEn / descriptionEn). Adds an English translation of the title and description of each tender (AI, faithful, no extra charge). Turn off to skip it. If the AI is not available in a run, the fields are null.

proMode.description: Pro mode (fit score, urgency, buyer profile, why-now, AI insight). One checkbox for the bid-decision extras on every tender: a 0-100 fit score with its reasons (how well it matches your keywords, sectors and UNSPSC codes, and whether there is time to bid), days to close and urgency (critical = 2 days or less, high = this week), a buyer profile from your own monitoring history (tenders this buyer published since you started monitoring and its typical budget), a dated 'why now' line and a one-sentence AI insight. Charged as an extra 'pro-result' event per tender (see Pricing).

priorityKeywords.description: Priority keywords (Pro). Words that matter most to you (also searched like normal keywords). In Pro mode a tender that mentions one gets +15 fit points. Example: ["licencias microsoft", "ciberseguridad"].

minFitScore.description: Minimum fit score (Pro). Pro mode only: tenders with a lower fit score are skipped and not charged. Leave empty to get every match ranked by fitScore.

monitorMode.description: Monitor mode (only new or changed tenders). For scheduled runs: remember what was found last time and output only tenders that are new, plus tenders you already received whose deadline was extended or moved, that were awarded (with winner and amount), cancelled, suspended or declared unsuccessful, or whose estimated amount changed. Each item gets changeType (new/changed) and a changes list. You pay only for new/changed tenders. Schedule it daily.

monitorStateName.description: Monitor state name. Optional name of the storage that keeps the previous results. Use the same name across scheduled runs to compare against them. Leave empty to derive it automatically from the rest of the input. Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only. Example: it-tenders-daily.

trackChanges.description: Re-check tenders already sent. Monitor mode: also re-check tenders you received before (that are not awarded/cancelled yet) for deadline extensions, awards, cancellations and amount changes, even if they no longer match the date window. Default on.

maxTrackedRechecks.description: Max tenders re-checked per run. Monitor mode: how many previously sent, still-open tenders are re-checked each run (oldest-checked first). Default 200. Re-checks are not charged; only real changes are.

notifyWebhookUrl.description: Webhook URL for alerts. Optional. When monitor mode finds new or changed tenders, POST a JSON summary to this URL (works with Zapier, Make, n8n; use it to send emails too). Example: https://hooks.zapier.com/hooks/catch/123/abc

notifySlackWebhookUrl.description: Slack webhook URL for alerts. Optional. Slack incoming-webhook URL to receive one line per new/changed tender (title, buyer, amount, deadline, link). Example: https://hooks.slack.com/services/T000/B000/XXXX

alertCountries.description:
Alert only for these countries. Monitor mode: send Slack/webhook alerts only for tenders from these countries (the dataset still has every new or changed tender, with alert = true/false). Example: ["CO", "PY"].
Options: CO = Colombia; BR = Brazil; CL = Chile; PY = Paraguay; UY = Uruguay.

alertSectors.description:
Alert only for these sectors. Monitor mode: alert only for tenders of these ready-made sectors (same ids as 'Sectors'). Example: ["medical", "it-software"].
Options: it-software = IT, software & computers; construction = Construction & public works; cleaning = Cleaning & facility services; security = Security & surveillance; medical = Medical supplies, drugs & lab; food = Food & catering; vehicles = Vehicles, parts, tyres & fuel; office-supplies = Office supplies & furniture; consulting = Consulting, audit & engineering studies; telecom = Telecom & connectivity; energy = Electrical, lighting & solar energy; events-travel = Events, travel & lodging; training-education = Training & education services; uniforms-ppe = Uniforms, workwear & PPE; waste-environment = Waste management & environment.

alertMinAmountUsd.description: Alert only above this amount (USD). Monitor mode: alert only for tenders whose estimated (or awarded) amount is at least this many US dollars. Tenders without a published amount do not alert. Example: 50000.

savedListName.description: Saved watchlist name. Give your keywords, sectors, UNSPSC codes, buyers and exclusions a name (e.g. my-it-watch) and the Actor remembers them: next runs (scheduled or not) use the saved list plus anything you add. Pair it with Monitor mode.

saveList.description: Save new items to the list. Add this run's keywords, sectors, codes, buyers and exclusions to the saved list (off = use the saved list without changing it).

inputSchema.description: Search new public tenders (licitaciones / licitações) in Colombia (SECOP II), Brazil (PNCP), Chile (Mercado Público), Paraguay (DNCP) and Uruguay (ARCE) by sector, keywords, UNSPSC code, buyer, region, amount, status and dates — or look up tenders by ID. Output is one normalized format for every country. Each tender returned is one dataset item and one charged result. Monitor mode outputs only new tenders and relevant changes (deadline extended, awarded, cancelled, amount changed).

instructions: Five data tools (live company jobs, company enrichment from a website, App Store & Google Play reviews, FMCSA US carriers, Latin American public tenders). Listing is free; running a tool needs APIFY_TOKEN and is billed per valid result on the user's Apify account.
